'''''Kalanchoe fedtschenkoi''''', formerly known as '''''Bryophyllum fedtschenkoi''''', is a species of flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae. It is native to [[Madagascar]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=''Kalanchoe fedtschenkoi'' Raym.-Hamet & H.Perrier|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:274335-1|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-14|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=Kew Science}}</ref> It is widely sold as a house or garden plant<ref name="titan">[http://titanarum.uconn.edu/198800251.html Bryophyllum fedtschenkoi (Raym.-Hamet & H.Perrier)], Connecticut University.</ref> that has established itself in the wild in some southern parts of the [[United States of America]]. The specific epithet ''fedtschenkoi'' honors botanist [[Boris Fedtschenko]] (1873-1947).<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/22992#page/101/mode/1up Raymond-Hamet & H. Perrier de la Bâthie. Annales du Museé Colonial de Marseille, sér. 2 3: 75–80. 1915.]</ref> Its genome has been sequenced as a model to study CAM metabolism.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=Xiaohan |last2=Hu |first2=Rongbin |last3=Yin |first3=Hengfu |last4=Jenkins |first4=Jerry |last5=Shu |first5=Shengqiang |last6=Tang |first6=Haibao |last7=Liu |first7=Degao |last8=Weighill |first8=Deborah A. |last9=Cheol Yim |first9=Won |last10=Ha |first10=Jungmin |last11=Heyduk |first11=Karolina |last12=Goodstein |first12=David M. |last13=Guo |first13=Hao-Bo |last14=Moseley |first14=Robert C. |last15=Fitzek |first15=Elisabeth |date=2017-12-01 |title=The Kalanchoë genome provides insights into convergent evolution and building blocks of crassulacean acid metabolism |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=1899 |doi=10.1038/s41467-017-01491-7  |doi-access=free|issn=2041-1723 |pmc=5711932 |pmid=29196618|bibcode=2017NatCo...8.1899Y }}</ref>

==Description==
''Kalanchoe fedtschenkoi'' is a low-growing, frost-tender perennial [[succulent]] which prefers dry, open ground. It grows to 10–12 inches (25–30 cm) tall as an untidy, low, rounded herb. The stems are round, smooth and lax with visible leaf scars, often bending and touching the ground where they produce roots and new plants. 

Leaves are fleshy, [[phyllotaxis|alternate]], blue-green and oval or [[Leaf shape|obovate]] with fine scalloped edges, the edges may turn pink or red under strong sunlight or drought conditions. Commonly called ‘Lavender Scallops’ from the shape and color of its leaves.<ref name="titan"/> Notably, the leaf surfaces exhibit water-repellent, self-cleaning properties that help protect the plant from insects and environmental pollutants. This behavior arises from a nanostructured, waxy surface architecture that imparts extremely low wettability, rendering the leaves superhydrophobic.<ref>{{cite journal

===Inflorescences=== 
The tubular flowers are in [[corymb]]s, often multi-layered in good conditions. Each flower has a short [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] edged with delta-shaped segments, which is shorter than its tubular [[Corolla (flower)|corolla]]. The corolla is an orange/coral/apricot color. The flowers are pendant.<ref name="efloras">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250092038 Bryophyllum fedtschenkoi], eFloras.</ref>
